The main takeaway from our work is that

ICSI-induced Ca2+ responses in the mouse egg are not a simple Ca2+ release but a series of Ca2+ oscillation, and that the Ca2+ oscillatory pattern is determined by the sperm factor that diffuses to the whole ooplasm and the Ca2+ release mechanism that generates propagating Ca2+.
the Ca2+ oscillation is a highly regulated process, and it is not simply a consequence of the release of a sperm factor.
